name: Rose
title: Rosa
ArtCultureRepresentation: Often used in contemporary digital art and photography to explore themes of beauty, decay, and the juxtaposition of romance and mortality.

name: Lily
title: Lilium
ArtCultureRepresentation: Featured in modern minimalist and surrealistic art to represent ethereal beauty and the fleeting nature of life, often contrasted with dark, moody backgrounds.

name: Sunflower
title: Helianthus annuus
ArtCultureRepresentation: A symbol of eco-art and climate change awareness, frequently used in large-scale installations to represent solar energy, optimism, and the Anthropocene era.

name: Lotus
title: Nelumbo nucifera
ArtCultureRepresentation: Heavily utilized in modern wellness art and neo-traditional tattooing, symbolizing the overcoming of struggle and the rise above digital noise.

name: Orchid
title: Orchidaceae
ArtCultureRepresentation: Represents the intersection of nature and technology in bio-art, often used in macro photography to highlight alien-like, synthetic aesthetics.

name: Cherry Blossom
Title: Prunus serrulata
ArtCultureRepresentation: Dominates contemporary anime, manga, and digital illustration as a visual shorthand for melancholic beauty, nostalgia, and the passage of time.

name: Tulip
title: Tulipa
description: Perfect love, deep forgiveness, and elegance
ArtCultureRepresentation: Used in pop art and modern still-life to critique consumerism, referencing the historical 'Tulip Mania' as a metaphor for modern cryptocurrency and economic bubbles.

name: Dandelion
title: Taraxacum
ArtCultureRepresentation: A popular motif in street art and contemporary illustration representing resilience, anti-establishment themes, and the organic dispersal of ideas.

name: Poppy
title: Papaver
ArtCultureRepresentation: Evokes powerful anti-war sentiments in modern protest art and muralism, transforming from a traditional symbol of death to one of peace, healing, and trauma awareness.

name: Hydrangea
title: Hydrangea macrophylla
ArtCultureRepresentation: Frequently used in fashion design and textile art for its voluminous, cloud-like forms, representing emotional depth and shifting perspectives in identity art.

name: Iris
title: Iris
ArtCultureRepresentation: Appears in Art Deco revivals and geometric abstract art, valued for its sharp, structural lines that bridge the gap between natural organic forms and architectural design.

name: Dahlia
title: Dahlia
ArtCultureRepresentation: Celebrated in modern maximalist art and pattern design for its complex, fractal-like geometry, symbolizing diversity, neurodivergence, and layered identities.

name: Marigold
title: Tagetes
artCultureRepresentation: Central to contemporary Día de los Muertos art and public murals, representing the vibrant, decaying threshold between the living and the dead.

name: Peony
title: Paeonia
ArtCultureRepresentation: Used in contemporary romanticism and luxury branding art, often rendered in thick impasto techniques to convey opulence, abundance, and tactile richness.

name: Chrysanthemum
title: Chrysanthemum
ArtCultureRepresentation: Featured heavily in dark academia and gothic-inspired contemporary art, representing the duality of life and death, and the beauty found in autumnal decay.
